walkthrough.title: Get started with Square Cloud
walkthrough.description: Deploy, follow and change your applications without leaving VS Code.
walkthrough.connect.title: Connect your account
walkthrough.connect.description:
Click **Connect account**, paste the 8-character code on the page that opens in your browser, and approve. VS Code never sees your password. The authorization stays in your system keychain for 90 days, and you can revoke it anytime in My account › Security.
[Connect account](command:squarecloud.setApiKey)
walkthrough.connect.alt: VS Code shows an 8-character code, you paste it on the approval page in your browser, and approve.
walkthrough.sidebar.title: Find everything in the sidebar
walkthrough.sidebar.description:
The Square Cloud sidebar lists your applications and databases with their live status, plus your Blob storage. Pick a workspace at the top to see a team's applications, add the ones you use most to favorites to keep them first, and hover over a row to start, stop or restart it. Click a row to open its panel; ⋯ has the rest.
[Open the sidebar](command:workbench.view.extension.squarecloud-container)
walkthrough.sidebar.alt: The sidebar with the account's memory, a workspace picker and application rows; hovering one shows start, restart and stop.
walkthrough.config.title: Describe your application in squarecloud.app
walkthrough.config.description:
To upload from VS Code, put a **squarecloud.app** file at the root of your project. It says which file starts the application, how much memory to reserve, the runtime version and, for a website, its subdomain.
As you type, the extension completes every key (Ctrl+Space), flags invalid values with a quick fix, and explains a key when you hover over it.
[Open the reference](https://docs.squarecloud.app/en/getting-started/config-file)
walkthrough.config.alt: A squarecloud.app file in the editor, with a hover that explains the MEMORY key.
walkthrough.upload.title: Upload or commit
walkthrough.upload.description:
**Upload** zips a project folder, leaving out what squarecloud.ignore lists, and creates a new application from it. Its panel opens when it's done.
**Commit** sends files or a folder to an application you already have, keeping its ID and address.
[Upload an application](command:squarecloud.uploadApplication)
[Commit files](command:squarecloud.commitEntry)
walkthrough.upload.alt: A project folder is zipped and sent to Square Cloud.
walkthrough.panel.title: Open an application
walkthrough.panel.description:
Each application opens in a panel of its own. **Overview** shows live CPU, memory and network, with start, stop and restart. **Metrics** charts the last 24 hours, or 7 days on Pro and Enterprise from 512 MB. **Deploys** links a GitHub repository so every push deploys, **Variables** edits the environment, and a website gets a **Network** tab with its traffic, domains, errors and performance.
[Open metrics](command:squarecloud.metricsEntry)
[Restart an application](command:squarecloud.restartEntry)
walkthrough.panel.alt: An application panel with its tabs, four live stats and a metrics chart.
walkthrough.logs.title: Follow logs live
walkthrough.logs.description:
The **Logs** tab loads the latest lines and keeps following new ones as your application prints them. Search, pause, clear the view or download what's on screen.
[Open logs](command:squarecloud.logsEntry)
walkthrough.logs.alt: A console with its newest line marked as live, a search field and a pause button.
walkthrough.files.title: Edit files in VS Code
walkthrough.files.description:
The **Files** tab lists your application's files. Each one opens in a regular VS Code editor, and saving writes it back to Square Cloud. Create, rename, upload or delete files there, or pick **Open as folder** to add the whole application to your workspace.
[Open the sidebar](command:workbench.view.extension.squarecloud-container)
walkthrough.files.alt: An application's file tree beside an editor; saving sends the file back to Square Cloud.
walkthrough.snapshots.title: Back up with snapshots
walkthrough.snapshots.description:
A snapshot is a copy of your application's files. Create one before a risky change, download it as a .zip, or restore it from the **Snapshots** tab and follow the restore step by step.
[Download a snapshot](command:squarecloud.snapshotEntry)
[Restore a snapshot](command:squarecloud.snapshotRestoreEntry)
walkthrough.snapshots.alt: A timeline of snapshots, with an arrow that restores the application to an earlier one.
walkthrough.databases.title: Databases and Blob storage
walkthrough.databases.description:
Create a MongoDB, MySQL, PostgreSQL or Redis database: its panel has the connection details, the TLS certificate, password reset, metrics and snapshots. **Blob** keeps files behind public or private links; upload, browse and copy links from its panel.
[Create a database](command:squarecloud.createDatabase)
[Open Blob storage](command:squarecloud.openBlob)
walkthrough.databases.alt: An application connected to a database with a TLS certificate, beside a grid of Blob files.
walkthrough.agent.title: Use Square Cloud in agent mode
walkthrough.agent.description:
With your account connected, VS Code's agent mode can use Square Cloud's tools: ask in chat for an application's status or logs, or to restart it, and VS Code asks you before each change. The extension adds the Square Cloud MCP server on its own. Connected before 6.0? Reconnect from the sidebar to allow it.
[About the MCP server](https://docs.squarecloud.app/en/mcp/overview)
walkthrough.agent.alt: A chat in VS Code calling a Square Cloud tool through mcp.squarecloud.app/mcp.

dns.body: Add these records at your domain's DNS provider. Verification and the HTTPS certificate follow on their own.
dns.title: DNS configuration
dns.name: Name

fallback.title: Alternative: DCV delegation
fallback.body: Instead of the _acme-challenge TXT records, create only this CNAME. It never changes, and certificate renewals need no further DNS changes. Delete the _acme-challenge TXT records first: a CNAME can't share its name with other records.

empty.title: Records not ready yet
empty.body: That's normal right after adding the domain: the records take a few minutes to be ready. The list refreshes on its own every minute.

purge.body: Clears the copies the edge keeps of your site, so every visitor gets the latest version. Handy after a deploy.
purge.title: Cache purge
purge.done: Cache purge started. The global edge is already removing the old copies. It can take up to 10 seconds for every visitor to see the latest version of your site.

network.thin: Not enough traffic for the timeline

notWebsite.title: This application isn't a website
notWebsite.body: Analytics count the requests that reach a site's public address, and this application was deployed without web publication. To get them, deploy it again with web publication turned on. Its logs keep working.

panel.noPlanBody: Your account has no active plan. You can still view, download, delete and make your files private. To upload new files, subscribe to a plan.
panel.emptyBody: Images, videos, backups and assets, with a public or private link. You can also drag files onto this area.
panel.emptyFolderBody: Upload files to this folder, or drag them onto this area.
panel.deleteBody: There is no trash: deleted files cannot be recovered.
panel.notInPlanBody: Store files behind public or private links. Subscribe to a plan to upload your first one.
panel.subtitle: Files behind public or private links
panel.tempLinkBody: Anyone with the link can download the file until it runs out, and it can't be revoked on its own. Making one needs an active plan, and it stops working early if this VS Code connection is revoked.
panel.tooBigToDrop: Files over 90 MiB can't be dropped here. Use Upload files for {{NAMES}}.
